publications.title: DeMo: Decoupled Momentum Optimization
publications.publishedAt: 14th International conference on learning representations · Apr 23, 2026
publications.description: Scaling neural network training increasingly depends on synchronous data-parallelism, yet full-precision gradient all-reduce imposes a severe communication bottleneck. We propose Decoupled Momentum Optimization (DeMo), a drop-in replacement for any momentum-based optimizers that significantly reduces the communication bandwidth while maintaining convergence. DeMo (i) decouples local momentum updates, (ii) applies a fast orthonormal transform (e.g., DCT) followed by top-k sparsification, and (iii) reuses the momentum buffer as error feedback via momentum subtraction. This design reduces per-step communication by up to two orders of magnitude with minimal computational overhead. Experiments on 300M and 1B-parameter DeMo language models show DeMo transmits up to 85x less data per GPU than AdamW-DDP while achieving comparable loss and accuracy. DeMo is topology-agnostic and enables training across multi-datacenter or Ethernet-based setups

publications.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
publications.publishedAt: 12th International conference on learning representations · Aug 31, 2023
publications.description: Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) have been shown to effectively encode positional information in transformer-based language models. However, these models fail to generalize past the sequence length they were trained on. We present YaRN (Yet another RoPE extensioN method), a compute-efficient method to extend the context window of such models, requiring 10x less tokens and 2.5x less training steps than previous methods. Using YaRN, we show that LLaMA models can effectively utilize and extrapolate to context lengths much longer than their original pre-training would allow, while also surpassing previous the state-of-the-art at context window extension. In addition, we demonstrate that YaRN exhibits the capability to extrapolate beyond the limited context of a fine-tuning dataset. We publish the checkpoints of Llama 2 7B/13B fine-tuned using YaRN with 64k and 128k context windows at https://github.com/jquesnelle/yarn

publications.title: On the linkability of Zcash transactions
publications.description: Zcash is a fork of Bitcoin with optional anonymity features. While transparent transactions are fully linkable, shielded transactions use zero-knowledge proofs to obscure the parties and amounts of the transactions. First, we observe various metrics regarding the usage of shielded addresses. Moreover, we show that most coins sent to shielded addresses are later sent back to transparent addresses. We then search for round-trip transactions, where the same, or nearly the same number of coins are sent from a transparent address, to a shielded address, and back again to a transparent address. We argue that such behavior exhibits high linkability, especially when they occur nearby temporally. Using this heuristic our analysis matched 31.5% of all coins sent to shielded addresses.

publications.title: CVE-2016-1562: Unauthenticated “filter” parameter leads to customer information leak in the DTE Energy Insight app
publications.description: A vulnerability I discovered in an application published by DTE Energy allowed an authenticated user to access the account details of all other users of the application. The vulnerability was assigned a CVE identifier by CERT which led to the application being patched.

publications.title: Scheduling a conference to minimize attendee preference conflicts
publications.publishedAt: Proceedings of the 7th Multidisciplinary International Scheduling Conference · Aug 28, 2015
publications.description:
This paper describes a conference scheduling (or timetabling) problem where, at
the time of registration, participants indicate preferences for events within the conference
that they would like to attend. Based upon these preferences, an assignment of events to
rooms and time slots should be determined that minimizes the number of attendee preference
conflicts and satisfies a number of hard constraints. Ideally the schedule should be
constructed so that for most, or all, participants the events that they would like to attend are
assigned to different time slots. We show that our problem, and several variants of it, are
NP-hard. An integer programming model is developed to solve the problem and a computational
study of this model is performed on instances generated from real data. Improvements
to the model, including a symmetry breaking reformulation and a dualization of some hard
constraints, are shown to significantly improve solution times, making the problem tractable
for the desired real world application.

IBM provides technical support services to many large companies as part of its global operations. I provided support to a prominent client on the Mac technical support line. The role included the following duties:
Providing first level troubleshooting and support for hardware, software and network issues that arise in the course of the customers use of the Apple Mac range of desktop and portable computers. 
Assisted with creating new user accounts, installing, configuring and troubleshooting software.
Providing support for the diagnosis of hardware issues, instructions and advice on configuring both wired and wireless LAN's.
Assisting with Internet connectivity and DNS issues, connecting to shared drives on both Apple and Microsoft networks
Troubleshooting cloud based services and educating new users on how to operate the system. 
Assistance with customers account related enquiries, billing disputes and investigating possible instances of fraudulent activity on customer’s accounts.

Stellar Asia-Pacific provides call centre operations on behalf of Telstra Bigpond. My duties there included:
Creation of new accounts, troubleshooting problems with a customer’s activation of their broadband service and assisting customers with their billing enquiries. 
Maintaining the internal office network, coordinating upgrades to the network, new switches, controllers, servers and terminals, maintaining the local intranet including the sub domains for the office blogs, creating new user accounts in Microsoft Active Directory.
Performing troubleshooting for users who are having issues with their terminals and liaising with Telstra’s IT team on issues and faults arising on the Telstra network.

2 degrees mobile is a recent entrant to the New Zealand mobile phone market, providing strong competition in that sector. Employed as a T2 Customer Support Specialist, my duties were as follows:
Helpdesk and Service Assurance involved providing high level customer support for handset and network related technical issues, escalated complaints and account disputes as well as supervision of Tier 1 call centre agents when large volumes of call backs were required. 
Identifying areas of the business where we were receiving large numbers of enquiries, complaints or confusion by customers, and working with the Marketing, Core Network, IT and Sales teams to address customers’ needs with any new products and services or alterations to existing services required.
Also largely responsible for developing the training requirements for new contact centre agents, and thus worked closely with the HR and Continuing Development teams. 
Assisted the Call Centre & Network Operations Teams in developing new processes and procedures, including writing up official procedural documentation based on the given process requirements, business process flowcharts and liaising with other stakeholders.

Temporary contracted postion with Vodafone iHug in their Internet Sales team. Duties performed were:
Inbound sales and customer retention
Converting enquiries by potential customers into sales
Identify the reasons for existing customers desire to cancel their service and provide a mutually beneficial resolution for both the customers and the company.

Self employed small business venture. As the owner/operator my business invloved the following:

Running a small business repairing and reselling washing machines. 
Locating potentially repairable washing machines advertised online, purchasing, repairing and reselling online. 
Providing after sales care and warranty services. 
Online advertising
Book keeping and accounting

As a general customer support agent of Vodafone’s Mobile services division, my duties included:
Answering general enquiries and complaints.
First tier technical support, such as password resets, troubleshooting basic issues.
Addressing potential billing disputes.

Employed as a customer support agent for one of New Zealand’s major Insurance providers in their Home, Contents and Vehicles division, my duties were largely as follows:
Explaining the details of various policies to customers
Identifying opportunities for upselling Tower products
Filing the initial claims made by customers for further review by the claims team.
